metadata.title: OpenSpore type archaeology synthesis blueprint
metadata.purpose: Define the deterministic normalized schema and merge procedure for the final type-archaeology artifact without making binary, runtime, or knowledge-graph claims.
metadata.scope: Original Spore 3.1.0.22 binary, SDK/reference analysis, worker syntheses, and explicitly separated current OpenSpore comparisons.

baseline.rtti: No MSVC RTTI; vtable and SDK-structure evidence must remain explicitly qualified.

metadata.identity_policy: Evidence and identity confidence are separate. A name, vtable sequence, shared prefix, or current-source resemblance may establish a candidate or relationship without establishing a class identity.
metadata.determinism_policy: No timestamps, wall-clock values, random IDs, machine-specific paths, or process-dependent ordering. Hashes and IDs are derived only from pinned input bytes and canonical content.

primary_source_policy.binary_bytes: Highest authority for addresses, bytes, sizes, and machine-level structure; interpretation still requires analysis context.
primary_source_policy.runtime_observation: Highest authority for observed original-runtime behavior, but not for a universal class identity unless the observation establishes it.
primary_source_policy.analysis_snapshots: Authoritative for the corresponding pinned analysis snapshot, not for claims outside its coverage.
primary_source_policy.sdk: Authoritative for SDK names, declared structures, SDK-provided relationships, and SDK address aliases; not proof that a name is the only original type at an address.
primary_source_policy.worker_synthesis: Preserved as derived evidence and mapped to its source record; never silently promoted to primary evidence.
primary_source_policy.current_source: Comparison and reconstruction relevance only; never silently merged into original-binary identity or runtime behavior.

worker_artifacts.role: Corpus identity, authority policy, source inventory, coverage, and limitations.
Near-direct normalized source for simulator, state, types, fields, vtables, inheritance, lifecycle, and methods.
Gameplay entity and Cell-family normalized source.
Creature, model, and data-oriented normalized source.
World/planet taxonomy, layout, serialization, consumers, and comparison source.
Empire, space, player-state, registry, ownership, and disagreement source.
Editor/UI type catalog, inheritance, vtable, ownership, factory, and replaceability source.
Event/message, dispatch, producer/consumer, and serialization source.
Persistence, record layouts, serialization primitives, function map, dispatch, and runtime-status source.
Asset/content type, container, descriptor, handle, consumer, and serialization source.
Manager, registry, global service, pool, accessor, and replaceability source.
Selected vtable records, slots, field consumers, constructor/destructor patterns, and limits.
Global field-offset inventory, high-value offsets, shared layouts, and current-source comparison.
Cross-subsystem object lifecycle, global ownership, factory, pool, manager, registration, and cleanup source.
Family and alias graph, address-bearing trees, binary/shared-prefix relations, factories, call patterns, and contradictions.
Scored reconstruction relevance, domain summary, vtable interfaces, unknown unlockers, and non-goals.
Unresolved candidate layouts, record patterns, hot offsets, consumers, ownership boundaries, lifecycle, and vtable slots.

source_artifact_record_rules.source_record_ref: Prefer RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. If a worker has no pointer, use its stable record id and worker id; never invent a line number.
source_artifact_record_rules.raw_claim_preservation: Every extracted claim stores the original source status, confidence wording, and narrow claim text in EvidenceRecord.raw_claim.
source_artifact_record_rules.worker_derivation: A worker record may create one or more evidence records, but worker prose is not silently converted to primary binary evidence.
source_artifact_record_rules.provenance_completeness: Every non-metadata final record references at least one evidence record and one source record pointer.

limitations.statement: The executable has no MSVC RTTI; type identity is assembled from SDK symbols, vtable evidence, layout evidence, and xrefs rather than read from RTTI.
limitations.impact: No worker-derived type, base, or alias may be presented as compiler-proven RTTI identity.

limitations.statement: This blueprint is static synthesis. A runtime status in a worker remains a source claim and is not converted into a universal runtime observation.
limitations.impact: Runtime booleans, lifecycle phases, and serialization claims require explicit runtime scope and evidence.

limitations.statement: The pinned triage and xref snapshots are distinct analysis states; counts and observations must retain their snapshot scope.
limitations.impact: Do not compare counts as if they came from one atomic analysis run.

limitations.statement: Current OpenSpore source comparisons are reconstruction aids, not evidence of the original executable's identity or behavior.
limitations.impact: Current-source names and layouts remain comparison or reconstruction records.

limitations.statement: The selected vtable corpus is narrower than the global vtable inventory; absence from the worker records is not absence from the binary.
limitations.impact: Keep global counts as metrics and selected records as records; do not manufacture missing vtable rows.

limitations.statement: Different workers can use different names, scopes, and confidence vocabularies for the same address or offset.
limitations.impact: Merge identity only under the rules below; preserve every alternative and create a conflict record.

limitations.statement: SDK names, path names, and naming-only family members can be useful without proving an original runtime type.
limitations.impact: Set identity_status to naming_only or candidate and retain source scope on every related claim.

limitations.statement: This blueprint describes a deterministic merge; it does not execute new Ghidra queries, alter the binary, mutate the SQLite graph, or add a knowledge-graph import step.
limitations.impact: Any follow-up extraction is a separate phase and must preserve these provenance rules.

normalization_rules: Unicode-normalize names to NFC before comparison while preserving the original spelling in source_claim.
Trim leading and trailing whitespace for identity keys; collapse internal whitespace only for display-normalized aliases, never for binary or SDK exact names.
Case-fold only for matching keys when the source vocabulary is explicitly case-insensitive; retain case-sensitive exact aliases separately.
Normalize hexadecimal addresses to 0x-prefixed lowercase, fixed-width for the program pointer size, without converting unknown or SDK-only addresses.
Normalize numeric offsets to non-negative JSON integers when exact; retain source strings for hexadecimal or range notation.
Normalize path separators only in display aliases; do not use path equality alone to merge types.
Sort all arrays by stable IDs or by explicitly declared semantic keys, then by source record pointer.
Sort object keys lexicographically after the required top-level order is applied.

identity_key_rules.type: Use origin_class plus canonical namespace/name or stable source identity. Anonymous, numeric-content, and address-bearing records receive deterministic disambiguation tokens instead of a random UUID.
identity_key_rules.alias: Use owner type id plus alias kind, namespace, and exact alias value; alias kind is part of the key.
identity_key_rules.field: Use owner type id plus source field identity. Same name with different offsets becomes one field cluster with alternative offset claims, not a silent overwrite.
identity_key_rules.vtable: Use program address when a binary address exists; otherwise use source kind plus canonical type or source record id.
identity_key_rules.slot: Use vtable id plus zero-based slot index. The index must agree with offset and pointer width when both are known.
identity_key_rules.inheritance: Use derived type id, base type id, relation kind, and vtable or SDK scope.
identity_key_rules.lifecycle: Use subject id, phase, and canonical operation sequence or source record id when sequence is not established.
identity_key_rules.method: Use exact program entry address when known; otherwise use source kind plus canonical function identity.
identity_key_rules.evidence: Use source artifact hash, source record pointer, and canonical extracted claim.
identity_key_rules.question: Use normalized question text plus subject scope; retain all source question records.
identity_key_rules.conflict: Use conflict topic plus sorted observation content digests.

id_formats.alias_id: ALIAS:<sha256(owner_type_id + alias_kind + exact_alias) first 24 lowercase hex>
id_formats.vtable_id: VT:<8-digit lowercase binary address> or VT:<escaped source identity>
id_formats.inheritance_id: INH:<sha256(derived + base + relation_kind + scope) first 24 lowercase hex>
id_formats.lifecycle_id: LIFE:<sha256(subject + phase + canonical operation sequence or source id) first 24 lowercase hex>
id_formats.method_id: METHOD:<8-digit lowercase entry address> or METHOD:<escaped source identity>
id_formats.evidence_id: EV:<sha256(artifact hash + source pointer + canonical claim) first 24 lowercase hex>
id_formats.relevance_id: REL:<escaped type or interface id>:<escaped domain or classification>
id_formats.question_id: Q:<sha256(normalized question + subject scope) first 24 lowercase hex>
id_formats.conflict_id: CONFLICT:<sha256(topic + sorted observation digests) first 24 lowercase hex>

evidence_policy.source_level_preservation: source_level must retain the exact worker vocabulary, including APPROXIMATION and name-only variants. normalized_support is a separate derived field and cannot replace source_level.
evidence_policy.runtime_rule: Only evidence with observation_scope equal to original_runtime may set runtime_observed true. Static, SDK, current-source, and worker synthesis evidence cannot create a runtime observation.
evidence_policy.current_source_rule: Current-source evidence may populate reconstruction_relevance and comparison fields, never original_binary identity, original_binary layout, or original_runtime behavior.
evidence_policy.worker_evidence_rule: A worker claim is evidence only at the scope it declares. Its source record pointer, raw claim, and source status remain mandatory.
evidence_policy.confidence_rule: Normalize confidence only when the worker defines a mapping. If no mapping exists, preserve the source confidence and set normalized_support to UNKNOWN rather than inventing a numeric score.

fields.layout_claims: array<object> preserving source-reported size and layout alternatives
fields.semantic_claims: array<object> preserving source-reported roles and descriptions

invariants: A type with identity_status naming_only or candidate cannot be described as a confirmed original runtime type.
current_comparison and sdk_reference records remain separate from original_binary records unless a source explicitly establishes equivalence.
Every non-synthetic type has at least one evidence id and a source scope.

fields.offset: non-negative integer or canonical hex string

invariants: A field identity cluster preserves all reported offsets and types when sources disagree.
A field range or multi-offset source group is not split into arbitrary scalar fields unless the source provides disjoint exact member boundaries.
Offset and semantic meaning are separate claims and have separate conflict ids.
A global offset without an owner type is represented as a FieldRecord with a synthetic owner or a shared-layout type, never assigned to an unrelated type by proximity alone.
Structure confidence and identity confidence are separate fields.
A slot is never assigned to a vtable solely because its address falls in a nearby address range.
Selected vtable records are preserved as records; global vtable counts remain metrics rather than fabricated records.
slot_index equals offset divided by pointer_width when both are exact.
Conflicting slot targets remain target_claims alternatives and create a conflict.
A slot name is not a function identity unless the target address or explicit association is recorded.
A shared vtable prefix is a structural relation, not automatically language-level inheritance.
SDK-declared bases remain sdk_declared even if a binary relation is absent or weaker.
Composition, ownership, and mere field-layout similarity are not stored as inheritance without explicit relation evidence.

fields.operations: array<object> preserving source step order and step text

invariants: A source list of lifecycle stages is not reordered into a complete lifecycle unless the source establishes the sequence.
runtime_observed is true only for original-runtime evidence.
Ownership is retained as a claim and is not promoted from allocator, pool, or vtable presence alone.
SDK names, source labels, and current-source names are name claims, not automatic method identity.
The same address with multiple names has one MethodRecord and multiple name claims; address aliases are retained.
A decompiled body never implies a runtime observation.

fields.confidence: object with grade, score, and source wording where available
fields.source_record_ref: RFC 6901 pointer or stable source record reference
fields.location: object containing available path, line, address, offset, or symbol without invented values

invariants: The ten worker-15 reconstruction domains are the controlled domain vocabulary unless a source explicitly introduces a narrower sublabel.
Ownership and subsystem boundaries are claims, not consequences of naming.

fields.subject_id: type, method, vtable, or subsystem id

invariants: Reconstruction classification is not an original-binary confidence value.
Current-source resemblance never changes an original type's identity_status.
Equivalent questions may share question_id only when subject scope and meaning are identical; every source wording remains in source_question_refs.
Questions are retained even when a worker gives a likely answer.

ordered_steps.name: pin_inputs
ordered_steps.rule: Verify every worker JSON and Markdown hash, parse every JSON file, and record the source schema and top-level keys. Stop if a hash or parse result differs.

ordered_steps.name: create_evidence
ordered_steps.rule: Create evidence records from source-native claims and locators before merging records. Retain source wording, source level, scope, and worker pointer.

ordered_steps.name: normalize_identity
ordered_steps.rule: Normalize names, addresses, offsets, paths, and IDs according to canonicalization_rules. Preserve exact source values in raw_claim and source_record_refs.

ordered_steps.name: build_aliases
ordered_steps.rule: Index aliases by owner and alias kind. Exact and qualified aliases may attach; ambiguous, address-only, naming-only, and current-source aliases remain qualified.

ordered_steps.name: build_types
ordered_steps.rule: Create one type per identity namespace, including SDK-only, naming-only, shared-layout, global-state, and candidate records. Do not merge across origin_class without explicit equivalence evidence.

ordered_steps.name: build_fields
ordered_steps.rule: Create field clusters and offset/type/access/semantic claim arrays. Never discard a competing offset, size, owner, or type claim; create conflicts where they disagree.

ordered_steps.name: build_vtables_and_slots
ordered_steps.rule: Normalize selected vtable addresses, validate pointer-width math, create slot records, and preserve candidate structure and identity status separately.

ordered_steps.name: build_relations
ordered_steps.rule: Build inheritance and lifecycle records from explicit relation and lifecycle evidence. Shared prefixes, layouts, ownership, and composition remain separate relation kinds.

ordered_steps.name: build_methods
ordered_steps.rule: Index methods by exact address first, then add SDK-only or source-labelled functions without inventing addresses. Merge names as claims and keep address aliases.

ordered_steps.name: build_semantics_and_reconstruction
ordered_steps.rule: Map subsystem and reconstruction records by stable subject references. Current-source and worker recommendations do not modify original-binary identity.

ordered_steps.name: retain_questions_and_conflicts
ordered_steps.rule: Deduplicate only semantically identical questions or observations. Keep every source wording, alternative, and unresolved status in the merged records.

ordered_steps.name: compute_metrics
ordered_steps.rule: Compute final canonical counts after merge, preserve worker/source counts as source_metric_refs, and report unknown populations as null or unknown rather than as zero.

ordered_steps.name: validate_and_sort
ordered_steps.rule: Validate referential integrity, schema order, IDs, source hashes, evidence coverage, and deterministic sorting. Emit no generated timestamp.

authority_merge_rules.when: Two records have exact canonical identity, same origin_class, and compatible alias evidence.
authority_merge_rules.action: Merge record fields and union source pointers and evidence; do not discard differing descriptions.

authority_merge_rules.when: Names match but namespace, owner, origin class, address, or semantic scope differs.
authority_merge_rules.action: Keep separate records, create aliases only with ambiguous or contextual equivalence, and create a conflict if workers assert one identity.

authority_merge_rules.when: Same field identity has different offsets, sizes, types, or owners.
authority_merge_rules.action: Cluster by field identity, retain all offset_claims/type_claims, and create a conflict. Use authority precedence only for a separately marked preferred claim.

authority_merge_rules.when: Vtable records share an address but disagree on slot count, boundary, target, or candidate type.
authority_merge_rules.action: Merge address-level structure, retain slot target alternatives, and preserve conflicts.

authority_merge_rules.when: A relation is supported by SDK declaration, shared binary prefix, or source assertion.
authority_merge_rules.action: Store relation_kind and evidence scope. Do not convert candidate_shared_base or binary_shared_prefix into language_level inheritance.

authority_merge_rules.when: A worker marks behavior as observed, confirmed, or runtime_validated.
authority_merge_rules.action: Retain source wording. Set normalized observation_scope only from an explicit original-runtime source; otherwise set runtime_observed false.

authority_merge_rules.when: A record comes from current OpenSpore source comparison.
authority_merge_rules.action: Store as current_comparison or reconstruction_relevance. Do not use it to confirm original identity, layout, ownership, or behavior.

authority_merge_rules.when: A candidate layout, pattern, slot, ownership boundary, or question has no decisive identity or runtime evidence.
authority_merge_rules.action: Keep the candidate or question, set candidate/unknown status, and preserve its source evidence and limits.

worker_specific_extraction.WA-00: Copy corpus identity, source inventory, authority precedence, conflicts, and limitations into metadata/provenance/limitations. Do not turn research leads into final type claims.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-01_WA-03: Use direct types, fields, vtables, inheritance, lifecycle, methods, consumers, evidence, semantic subsystem, reconstruction relevance, and unresolved questions. Shared_state becomes synthetic global fields or subsystem records.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-04: Map taxonomy, terrain/climate/geography, world_model, ownership_lifecycle, serialization, and reconstruction records. Keep current_openspore_comparison separate.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-05: Map type_registry to types/aliases, vtable_families to vtables/inheritance, shared_player_state to fields or synthetic global types, and disagreements to conflicts.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-06: Map type_catalog, inheritance_and_vtables, ownership_lifecycle, factories_and_serialization, and consumers_and_flows. Keep replaceability as reconstruction relevance and contradictions as conflicts.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-07: Map types, functions, dispatch_lifecycles, producer_consumer_relationships, serialization, semantic_ownership, and evidence catalogs. Preserve event semantics separately from method identity.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-08: Map record_layouts and serialization primitives to types/fields/aliases; function_map to methods; vtables_and_dispatch to vtables/slots; lifecycle to lifecycle; runtime status remains scoped evidence.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-09: Map content_types, container_layouts, descriptors, handles, vtables_and_classes, consumer_graph, serialization, and reconstruction relevance. Numeric content types remain values or aliases, not C++ class identity.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-10: Map accessors to methods, global service slots to fields/slots, registries/containers/pools to types and lifecycle, and replaceability to reconstruction relevance.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-11: Map selected vtable_records to vtables and slots, field_offsets_and_vtable_consumers to field evidence, inheritance_chains to inheritance, and constructor/destructor patterns to lifecycle/method claims. Preserve selected coverage limits.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-12: Map high_value_offsets and shared_layouts to fields/types and reconstruction comparison. Do not assign global offsets to nearby owners without source evidence.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-13: Map object_lifecycles and lifecycle_stages to lifecycle, global_ownership/managers/registrations to ownership and subsystem claims, factories to methods, pools/cleanup/exception paths to lifecycle, and contradictions to conflicts.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-14: Index all families and naming_only_families, aliases_and_duplicate_identities, address_bearing_family_trees, binary_inheritance_relations, common_bases, constructor_destructor_pairs, factories, and call_patterns. Keep naming-only and SDK-only identity distinct.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-15: Map assessments, domain_summary, quantitative_baseline, vtable_interfaces, interface_anchors, and unknown_unlockers to reconstruction_relevance, semantic_subsystems, and unresolved_questions.
worker_specific_extraction.WA-16: Map candidate_layouts, record_patterns, candidate_patterns, hot_offsets, consumer_clusters, lifecycle, ownership_boundaries, and vtable_slots as candidate, field, subsystem, lifecycle, and vtable evidence. Keep unknowns explicit.

coverage_policy.include_all_worker_records: Every substantive type, alias, field, vtable, slot, inheritance, lifecycle, method, evidence, subsystem, relevance, question, conflict, and metric record present in the 17 worker JSON files is either represented or explicitly listed in a coverage disposition.
coverage_policy.selected_vtables: Import all selected vtable records in WA-11 and all explicit vtable/slot records in other workers. Report the global 3,081-vtable inventory as a metric, not as unpersisted rows.
coverage_policy.class_families: Index all 1,250 families and all 1,199 naming-only families in WA-14 as type/alias records, with source status and identity status preserved.
coverage_policy.large_corpora: Do not summarize away records needed for exact final counts. If a source stores a family or assessment as a scalar, preserve the scalar as evidence and create a source coverage disposition.

structural_rules: The target JSON has exactly the declared top-level keys in target_top_level_order.
Every final record ID is unique within its namespace and matches its declared format.
Every referenced record ID exists and has the same kind expected by the reference.
Every record contains at least one evidence_id, except top-level metadata, provenance, and derived metric diagnostics.
Every evidence_id resolves to an EvidenceRecord whose source_artifact_sha256 matches the pinned worker or primary source.
Every source_record_ref resolves to a JSON Pointer or explicitly names a stable source record.
Every final array is sorted by the declared stable key and then by source_record_ref; no array order depends on map iteration or runtime query order.
All addresses are lowercase fixed-width hexadecimal, all unknown addresses are null, and all exact offsets use canonical numeric or hex representation.
All evidence references and conflict references are sorted and duplicate-free.
All source-level strings are preserved verbatim; normalized values are stored under separate fields.
No object contains a generated_at, timestamp, wall-clock field, random UUID, machine path, or process id.
No field or vtable relation is marked confirmed solely because a source says verified without a scope that supports confirmation.
No current-source record is referenced by an original_binary identity or runtime_observed=true claim.
semantic_rules: A binary_shared_prefix relation is not language-level inheritance.
A vtable's slot sequence does not prove the candidate type identity without independent evidence.
A shared field offset does not prove common ownership or inheritance.
A pool, manager, accessor, or factory does not prove exclusive ownership unless the source establishes it.
A decompiled method body does not prove original runtime behavior.
A candidate type, naming-only family, and confirmed type remain distinguishable by identity_status and origin_class.
Equivalent questions may be clustered only when subject scope and meaning are preserved.
Conflicting claims remain visible in conflict observations and in the affected record's claim arrays.
reconciliation_rules: For each worker top-level key, section_map has at least one target and the extraction disposition is recorded.
For each worker artifact, both JSON and Markdown hashes match provenance.worker_artifacts.
Final canonical counts are computed after all merge steps; source counts and selected-record counts remain separately named.
Metrics with unknown population use null, unknown, or an explicit unavailable status, never zero.
The final artifact can be regenerated byte-for-byte from the pinned worker bytes and this blueprint; no current filesystem enumeration is part of canonical output.

failure_policy.parse_or_hash_failure: Stop synthesis; do not emit a partial final artifact.
failure_policy.reference_failure: Stop synthesis; repair the extractor or preserve the record as unresolved.
failure_policy.contradiction: Continue only when all alternatives are retained and a conflict record is emitted; otherwise stop.
failure_policy.authority_tie: Preserve both observations with equal status; do not arbitrarily select a winner.

counts.name: Pinned function count
counts.notes: Retain as a baseline metric; final canonical function records are not required to equal this Ghidra inventory.

counts.name: Pinned xref count
counts.notes: Keep separate from canonical method or call-edge counts.

counts.name: Global vtable inventory
counts.notes: Selected worker vtable records are a separate coverage metric.

counts.name: Class-family corpus
counts.notes: Naming-only family count is tracked separately.

coverage.name: Worker artifacts mapped
coverage.notes: Each worker has a section map and extraction disposition.

coverage.name: Selected vtable records
coverage.notes: Does not imply 3,081 final vtable rows.

merge_diagnostics.count_policy: Count only records that pass structural validation; retain unknown populations as null or unknown.
merge_diagnostics.deduplication_policy: Deduplicate exact identity keys only; preserve source pointers, evidence, and conflicts for merged records.

metric_definitions.name: function_count
metric_definitions.definition: Number of functions in the pinned analysis snapshot; not the number of normalized MethodRecord rows.

metric_definitions.name: xref_count
metric_definitions.definition: Number of xref rows or xref edges in the pinned snapshot; deduplication rule must be stated separately.

metric_definitions.name: vtable_inventory
metric_definitions.definition: Global vtable inventory reported by the pinned analysis; distinct from selected worker vtable records.

metric_definitions.name: canonical_type_count
metric_definitions.definition: Number of unique TypeRecord ids after identity merge, including qualified SDK, candidate, and naming-only records.

metric_definitions.name: canonical_field_count
metric_definitions.definition: Number of unique FieldRecord identity clusters, not the number of offset alternatives.

metric_definitions.name: conflict_count
metric_definitions.definition: Number of unique ConflictRecord ids; observations are not counted as separate conflicts.
